newsitem.title: FINLAND: Moody's upgrade will support Finnish debt - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Moody's upgrade will support Finnish debt - dealers.

text.p: A Moody's upgrade of Finland's long-term foreign currency debt rating to Aa1 from Aa2 on Wednesday was good news but no surprise, and would help to narrow Finnish debt premiums over Germany, dealers said.

"The Finnish risk premium could fall slightly," said Ari Lahti, managing director at Protos brokerage. But the yield gap over Germany would not fall significantly from the current 33 basis points on this alone, he said.
"It was no surprise. But it is good news, a recognition that there is confidence in Finland, that economic policy is on track and the risk related to Finland is fading," Lahti said.
Another senior bond dealer, speaking on condition of anonymity, said an upgrade by Moody's had been "partly discounted".
"We have already had a sharp move lower, but long-end yields could ease a couple of basis points further (on the news)," he said.
A third senior bond dealer agreed that the upgrade was a "positive" piece of news.
